name: Roque de los Muchachos — MAGIC and CTAO-North
notes: Telescope footprints are OpenStreetMap ways (MAGIC I and II, LST-1, three newer LSTs), read with the OSM API map call on 2026-10-25 because Overpass answered 502 at capacity. The MAGIC separation (85 m) and the LST-1 distance from MAGIC ('~100 m') come from the joint LST-1/MAGIC paper (arXiv:2310.01954).

The three newer LSTs are not numbered in OSM or in any fetched source; they are named by OSM way. CTAO announced the inauguration of the four-LST sub-array on 2026-10-15 and says the telescopes will now be commissioned. All CTAO features inherit experiment:ctao's 'construction' status, so LST-1 (observing since 2018) is drawn with the same status as the new LSTs.

The planned CTAO-North layout (four LSTs and nine MSTs over about 0.5 km2) is published only as an unscaled figure; the nine MSTs are not drawn. OSM also maps FACT (a small Cherenkov telescope that is not an atlas entity) and many optical telescopes, which are not part of this facility's inventory.

schematics.note: Official CTAO layout figure with no scale bar or coordinate axes; shows the four LSTs, nine MSTs and the MAGIC telescopes. Topology only. Never drawn on the to-scale map.

summary.plain: The mountaintop observatory on La Palma, Canary Islands, with the two 17 m MAGIC gamma-ray telescopes and the four 23 m Large-Sized Telescopes of the northern Cherenkov Telescope Array.
summary.technical: Six telescope footprints and the MAGIC counting house from OpenStreetMap; the MAGIC-I to MAGIC-II distance is checked against the published 85 m, LST-1 against the published ~100 m from MAGIC. The outline is the convex hull of the six footprints. Map centre is CTAO-North's published array coordinate.
